title: Unify retry/timeout/backoff policies across runtime + SDKs; idempotency & hedged request guidelines
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: create a single, opinionated set of retry/timeout/backoff rules for Redwood services and official SDKs that balances SLO adherence, minimal duplicate side-effects, and predictable cost under degraded conditions. This includes standard headers and patterns for idempotency keys, a hedged-request policy for cross-region tail-latency mitigation, and guidance for circuit breakers and load-shedding that tie to our SLO + error budget model.
background: We have inconsistent retry behaviour across services and SDKs: some SDKs retry POSTs without idempotency, one-off ad-hoc backoff implementations, and regional failover logic duplicated in multiple places. This causes excess downstream load, unclear SLO ownership during incidents, and customer-visible duplicate side-effects. Recent incidents (see ENG-5675) showed cascading retries across regions causing error-budget exhaustion and slow recovery. We need a clear, small-surface specification plus an implementation in the runtime and SDKs.
technical_design:
High level rules:
1) Two-layer retry model: client-side (SDK) optimistic retries with strict idempotency checks + server-side defensive retry gates in the runtime.
2) Timeouts: per-request overall deadline + per-RPC connection timeout. Defaults: overall deadline = 8s, per-attempt timeout = 2s. Services with p95 SLO & low-latency obligations can override via config.
3) Retry counts: default max attempts = 2 (original + 1 retry), jittered exponential backoff base=150ms, multiplier=2, max_backoff=2s.
4) Idempotency: SDKs MUST expose an idempotency_key header (X-Redwood-Idempotency) for mutating endpoints. If empty and operation is non-idempotent, SDK will not retry automatically. Servers treat requests with idempotency keys deterministically: store outcome for 60s (configurable) and return cached response for duplicate keys.
5) Hedging: for requests expected to be p99-sensitive, SDKs may issue a hedged attempt after hedging_delay = 150ms if no response. Hedging is opt-in per-route and limited in-flight (global hedging concurrency per-region). Hedged requests set a header X-Redwood-Hedged: true and include same idempotency key.
6) Circuit breakers & load shedding: runtime will maintain per-route circuit states driven by five-minute error-rate and latency windows. Tripping thresholds are tied to SLOs (e.g., if error rate > 4x SLO error budget burn-rate over 5m). When tripped, runtime returns a lightweight 429 with Retry-After and signals SDKs to fallback.
7) Observability: each retry/hedge attempt must emit a structured event with attempt_number, attempt_latency_ms, idempotency_key, hedged=true/false, route, and outcome. Add dashboards for retry amplification and hedged request hit ratio.
8) Backwards compatibility: default behaviour is conservative (minimal retries for mutating endpoints). New SDK minor versions opt-in to hedging and idempotency enforcement.
rollout_plan:
1) Spec review with API owners + PM (week 0). 2) Runtime feature flags: implement server-side idempotency cache and defensive retry gates behind FF (week 1). 3) SDK changes (js/py/go): expose idempotency key param + conservative client retries behind opt-in flags; release minor versions (week 2). 4) Enable hedging only for a small set of high-P95 routes (canary 5% traffic) and monitor amplification metrics (week 3). 5) Ramp to 25% then full for routes meeting criteria; migrate other teams with API owner sign-off (week 4+). 6) Documentation and examples for customers and design notes in Confluence.
Canary controls: runtime will allow per-team route flags; SDKs default hedging disabled until runtime signals capability. Rollback: disable hedging FF or set runtime hedging concurrency to 0.
acceptance_criteria:
- A single RFC-style spec merged to docs/confluence specifying headers, defaults, and operational knobs.
- Runtime: idempotency cache implemented and returning cached responses for duplicate keys within TTL.
- SDKs: js/py/go publish minor versions that surface idempotency_key and default conservative retries.
- Hedging: enabled in canary for at least one route and we have graphs showing no duplicate side-effects and <5% retry amplification.
- Dashboards: retry amplification, hedged_request_ratio, idempotency_cache_hit_rate, per-route circuit state.
- Chaos tests: injected latency scenario shows hedging reduces tail latency without increasing customer-visible errors.
- Security review completed (if idempotency affects auth flows).
test_plan:
Unit tests for SDK idempotency header generation and non-retry behaviour on mutating ops without key. Integration tests: simulate duplicate requests with same idempotency key and verify cached response. Load tests: ensure retries do not double the RPS beyond acceptable thresholds under partial outage. Chaos: region failover + latency injection to verify hedged requests improve p99. Observability tests: synthetic traffic to assert correct metrics emitted.
Add e2e tests in CI that flip feature flags for hedging and ensure fallbacks behave as expected (429 handling and Retry-After adherence).
risks_and_mitigations:
Risk: Duplicate side-effects if idempotency not used correctly or cached state lost. Mitigation: conservative defaults (no automatic retry for mutating ops unless idempotency key present) and short idempotency TTL.
Risk: Hedging increases load and can amplify failures. Mitigation: hedging is opt-in per-route with global concurrency caps, monitor amplification metrics, automatic cutoff if retry amplification > threshold.
Risk: SDK adoption lag. Mitigation: fallback server-side defensive gates and compatibility mode; include migration checklist for partner teams.
Risk: Operational complexity in debugging (multiple attempts). Mitigation: structured attempt tracing + correlation id and single-line dashboard views for request chains.
open_questions:
- TTL for server-side idempotency cache for long-running ops (>1s) vs short ops? (proposal: 60s default, override per-route).
- Should hedging be allowed for multi-step transactions or only single-shot read-like calls?
- How to handle authorization tokens that expire between hedged attempts? (proposal: SDKs should tie hedged attempts to current valid token and fail-safe if token refresh occurs).
- Should we expose a top-level SDK flag to disable all client-side retries for customers that want to manage retries externally?
decisions:
- Default max attempts = 2 and per-attempt timeout = 2s (conservative by default).
- Introduce X-Redwood-Idempotency header as standard.
- Hedging is opt-in per-route and requires idempotency keys for mutating routes.
- Circuit breaker thresholds will be tied to configured SLO/Error-budget windows rather than fixed error percentages.
